topics: SAML SSO setup (metadata, cert rotation, NameID, attributes)
SCIM provisioning and deprovisioning (group sync, rate limits)
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-11-18 16:00 PST | Duration: ~54 min | Attendees: Priya (Redwood AE), Daniel (Redwood SE), Lisa (Meridian - Head of IT), Marco (Meridian - Security Architect), Aisha (Meridian - IAM)

[00:00] Priya (Redwood AE): hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm priya from redwood, i'll kick us off. objective today is to walk through sso + scim setup and the rbac model, make sure it meets meridian's least-privilege requirements and compliance guardrails
[00:18] Lisa (Meridian): thanks, yes we want to confirm we can federate with our okta tenant, have SCIM provisioning for users and groups, and ensure audit logs are accessible for our internal siem. also curious about encryption at rest and key management options
[00:32] Daniel (Redwood SE): great, i'll go deep on the technical bits — metadata exchange, assertion attributes, cert rotation, and how scim handles group syncs and deprovisioning. quick note — transcription may have small errors, i'll try to be explicit.
[01:05] Marco (Meridian): our timeline is tight: security review this week, infra sign-off next week, pilot the week after. success criteria: SSO working with MFA through our okta, SCIM provisioning of 2k users and group mappings, and logs exported to splunk.
[01:28] Priya: perfect. quick overview: redwood supports sso via saml 2.0 (sp-initiated + idp-initiated), scim 2.0 for provisioning, group-sync, and fine-grained rbac that maps to saml groups or scim groups. for enterprise we provide vpc/private options and kms integration for key management.
[02:05] Lisa: do you support encrypted assertions and signed responses? we require signed assertions and prefer encrypted if possible.
[02:12] Daniel: yes — we support signed assertions and encrypted assertions. our typical config: we consume the idp cert for signature validation; we can also accept encrypted assertions if you share your public encryption key. note on behavior: some idps (okta) require the sp metadata to have the encryption algorithm indicated.
[02:40] Aisha: what about nameid format? we use persistent nameid and email attribute mapping, groups come in as saml attribute 'groups' for us.
[02:50] Daniel: recommended pattern is NameID = email (or persistent if your privacy policy requires it) and then include groups as a multi-valued attribute. we also support mapping custom attributes (employeeId, dept). when mapping to rbac, we prefer group->role mapping on the redwood side to keep least-privilege central.
[03:22] Marco: certificate rollover — how do you handle rotation without breaking sessions?
[03:28] Daniel: we support dual-cert metadata (you can upload a new cert and keep the old one valid for X days), and we accept idp-initiated metadata refresh. for hosted customers we assist with cert rollover plans and can automate rotation if you want. just one gotcha: if you enable encrypted assertions, both sides need to be coordinated for the encryption key change window.
[04:10] Lisa: SCIM — does redwood support incremental updates or only full sync? we have ~2k accounts, frequent org changes, need fast deprovisioning for offboarding.
[04:21] Daniel: scim 2.0 supports both provisioning and delta (incremental) changes. we support PATCH for incremental changes and also bulk operations (with rate limits). our recommendation: use group-based provisioning — provision groups via SCIM and map groups to redwood roles. deprovisioning honors the 'active' attribute; we also provide an admin-level webhook and SCIM event logs so you can reconcile.
[05:00] Marco: rate limits — what's safe? our provisioning will be bursty during initial sync.
[05:07] Daniel: we publish a rate limit in the admin console; typical is 600 requests/min for scim on enterprise dedicated. for large initial syncs we can coordinate a temporary bump or use our bulk import API to avoid hitting rate limits. we'll note this in docs.
[05:45] Aisha: group sync cadence — we want near-real time for critical groups, can you do push-based?
[05:52] Daniel: SCIM is effectively pull from the SP but with PATCH events it's near real-time from the idp side, many idps (eg okta) push changes to our scim endpoint as users change. if you need instant push, we can also integrate a provisioning webhook to notify your systems.
[06:30] Lisa: RBAC mapping — give me the model. we want least-privilege by default and a small set of admin roles.
[06:38] Daniel: redwood has built-in roles (viewer, developer, admin, infra-admin). you can create custom roles scoped to routes, models, or org-level admin. mapping pattern: map low-privilege groups to viewer/developer roles, map a small group for infra-admin that can do VPC/peering/config. we recommend two-step approach: 1) scim/groups -> redwood roles; 2) use an approval workflow for promotion to admin (manual or integrated with your approval system).
[07:25] Marco: can we enforce least-privilege at token level (temporary tokens, short-lived creds)?
[07:30] Daniel: yes, tokens have TTLs; for programmatic access we recommend short TTLs with refresh via your own token broker. for human UI access we support sso session durations and can enforce reauth/mfa policies based on saml assertions (we respect your sessionTimeOut values).
[08:05] Lisa: audit logs — what fields do you capture and how long are they retained? we need exports to splunk with JSON schema, and typical retention for us is 12 months internally.
[08:15] Priya: we capture token-level usage, per-route/model request logs, admin actions (role changes, scim provisioning events), and security events (failed logins, cert changes). retention depends on plan — default 90 days for hosted, extended for enterprise (we can do 365+). exports: we support push to S3, syslog, splunk HEC, or streaming via kinesis. logs are structured JSON and include request_id, user_id, source_ip, action, model, token_type, and timestamp.
[09:05] Marco: any PII in logs? we need to avoid leaking user content.
[09:10] Daniel: we do not include request content by default in audit logs. content-level logging is opt-in and masked; for enterprise we can configure redaction rules and run content-only exports under NDA.
[09:45] Aisha: encryption — at rest and in transit? kms? hsm?
[09:50] Daniel: data in transit is TLS 1.2/1.3. at rest we use AES-256; for customer-managed keys we integrate with KMS (aws kms, gcp kms) and can support HSM-backed keys for dedicated/private deployments. for private on-prem we can integrate with your HSM. we also support envelope encryption for model artifacts.
[10:30] Lisa: data residency — can we keep logs and inference data in our region?
[10:36] Priya: yes, for enterprise we offer region-specific tenancy. hosted accounts can select region for data storage; dedicated/private gives full control (VPC, on-prem). we'll document which components are region-bound (control plane vs data plane).
[11:05] Marco: compliance artifacts — SOC2/ISO scope and frequency?
[11:12] Priya: we have SOC2 type II and ISO 27001 certificates; attestation reports are available under NDA. our SOC2 scope includes infrastructure, platform, and access controls for hosted customers; for dedicated/private we provide additional docs about network segmentation and deployment boundaries.
[11:40] Lisa: ok we will need SOC2 report and a mapping to our control requirements (we'll supply questionnaire).
[11:46] Priya: absolutely — i'll send the SOC2 and iso artifacts and a control mapping template.
[12:05] Marco: one more technical question: single logout (slo) — does redwood support it? we have complex session flows.
[12:12] Daniel: we support saml single logout but caveats: not all idps implement slo reliably, and slo for short-lived api tokens is different than browser sessions. recommended approach: rely on scim deprovisioning + short token TTLs for programmatic access and use slo for UI sessions only.
[12:50] Aisha: monitoring and alerting for suspicious activity?
[12:55] Daniel: we provide anomaly detection hooks — e.g., sudden spike in token usage, repeated failed assertions. we can push alerts to pagerduty/webhook and include detailed event context.
[13:20] Priya: circling back to rbAC: can we have nested groups and role inheritance?
[13:26] Daniel: redwood supports nested group flattening when scim provides nested structures. for rbac we evaluate flattened group membership, then apply role precedence rules (explicit deny > explicit allow). we can show you the precedence table.
[14:05] Lisa: how do we test? what's the recommended runbook for an sso pilot?
[14:12] Daniel: proposed pilot runbook: (1) exchange SAML metadata (idp <-> sp) in a dev okta org; (2) configure scim with a small test group of 10 users; (3) verify assertions, group attribute mapping, and cert verification; (4) test deprovisioning via 'active=false'; (5) validate audit log generation and splunk export; (6) test cert rollover. typical pilot takes 2-3 days once metadata is exchanged.
[15:02] Marco: any gotchas we've seen in the field?
[15:08] Daniel: yes — timezone/skew in assertion timestamps causes validation errors (clock skew), ensure clocks are synced. also attribute naming (groups vs roles) differs between idps; confirm exact attribute name. cert formatting differences (pem vs der) sometimes trip up automated tools. lastly, scim group size limits — some idps chunk groups and send partial payloads.
[15:55] Lisa: regarding logs to splunk, do you push full activity or do we pull?
[16:00] Priya: both supported: you can configure push to splunk HEC or S3 export + ingestion. for real-time security use cases we recommend direct HEC. we'll provide sample HEC config and a sample JSON log schema.
[16:30] Aisha: can we restrict certain users from exporting logs or changing rbac mappings? we need separation of duties.
[16:36] Daniel: yes — admin roles are scoped; for example only infra-admin can configure vpc/peering and log sinks, and only org-admin can change billing. role assignments can be constrained to specific groups and require approval for elevation.
[17:05] Marco: do you have an audit trail for admin role changes?
[17:10] Daniel: yes, admin changes are logged with before/after, who initiated, and we support export of those events to your siem.
[17:36] Lisa: what's the onboarding friction for our end users? we prefer idp-initiated flow so users click 'redwood' in okta and single sign on.
[17:43] Daniel: idp-initiated is supported; both flows are fine. ensure your okta app is configured with the correct assertion consumer service url from our sp metadata. we'll provide the metadata xml.
[18:10] Priya: timeline check — we said infra sign-off next week. who owns metadata exchange?
[18:16] Lisa: aisha will handle okta side and marco will provide infra details.
[18:20] Aisha: ok i'll do the metadata exchange and test with 2 dev users.
[18:28] Priya: action items recap coming in the notes. we'll also send a scim sample payload and a rbAC mapping template.
[18:40] Marco: one last security item — do you support customer-managed key rotation logs? we need to show key rotation history.
[18:48] Daniel: for KMS integrations we can provide a rotation audit trail and show key versions. for hsm-backed deployments we can include attestation logs.
[19:10] Lisa: perfect. any blockers on your side for a pilot?
[19:15] Priya: none — just need the idp metadata and an okta dev org to test against. we'll also request an IP allowlist for the scim endpoint if you want to restrict to meridian's outbound egress.
[19:45] Aisha: we'll provide the allowlist and create a dev okta app this afternoon.
[20:00] Priya: cool. closing notes: we'll send docs and task owners. thanks everyone.

[21:00] (end of recorded highlights)

Notes: transcript has minor stutters and name mis-attributions possible. references to 'okta' as example idp; meridian uses Okta in their environment. Shared artifacts referenced during call: SOC2 report (link sent under NDA), SP metadata (to be shared), SCIM sample payload (to be shared), RBAC mapping template (to be shared).
